verdicts.rationale: Fully traced and confirmed. On a freshly-opened, never-edited doc `latestDoc` is null: it is set ONLY inside the 300ms debounce of editor-ops.ts handleUpdate (lines 45-48), and that handler is wired to TipTap's onUpdate (Editor.tsx:796-798) which does NOT fire when content is provided at creation via the `content: initialContent` option (Editor.tsx:462, immediatelyRender:false). Verified there is no other setLatestDoc call anywhere (grep: only editor-ops.ts). So docForOutline=latestDoc=null → outlineHeadings=[] and outlineTotalBlocks=0 (EditorLayout.tsx:2360-2362). Meanwhile the OUTLINE PANEL renders real rows because its `content` prop is the LIVE editor.getJSON() (EditorPane.tsx:3400/3473) fed into extractHeadings(content) (OutlinePanel.tsx:1516) — confirming the live-vs-debounced split. activate([],0) reads the live doc (useFocusMode.ts:260, non-null) but takes the headings.length===0 branch → start=0,end=-1 (lines 264-268) → bandFromIndices(doc,0,-1): startUuid=null (startIdx<=0), endUuid=uuidOfIndex(doc,-1)=null (line 86 returns null for i<0) → {active:true,startUuid:null,endUuid:null}; resolveFocusBand resolves null/null to {0,lastIdx}=whole doc (focus-view.ts:115-116). moveTo(idx,[],0)→sectionRange(idx,[],0) returns [0,-1] (line 144) → same whole-doc band. Both repro paths confirmed. Severity MEDIUM held (not HIGH): focus is a non-destructive view feature, the bug is fully recoverable (self-heals after the first edit settles), and no user content is touched — but it misfires on EVERY pristine open, so above LOW.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: The focus engine is fed structure derived from the 300ms-debounced `latestDoc` snapshot (EditorLayout.tsx:2360-2362 via useFocusActions/focus.ts:21-38) while every render-time consumer reads the live editor.getJSON(); `latestDoc` is never seeded on editor-ready, only inside the onUpdate debounce (editor-ops.ts:45-48), and TipTap onUpdate never fires on initial content load (Editor.tsx:462,796). The empty-list path collapses to a whole-doc band (useFocusMode.ts:264-268 + bandFromIndices:110-111 + resolveFocusBand:115-116).
verdicts.class: Consumers that derive document structure from the debounced `latestDoc` rather than the live editor, all empty/wrong until the first edit settles: availableDividerLevels/activeDividerLevels (EditorLayout.tsx:2363-2374 — divider menu empty on pristine doc) and focusWordCount (EditorLayout.tsx:2387-2392, reads docForOutline). Same live-vs-debounced snapshot split flagged for the post-edit window in the sibling g-anchor finding.

verdicts.rationale: Real, and the no-structural-bump mechanism is verified, but the finder missed an incidental masking path that materially changes WHEN the staleness is observable — hence reclassified (corrected cause), severity unchanged at MEDIUM. Verified: useStructuralRevisions subscribes to NO content-change event (useStructuralRevisions.ts:93-128 has onHeadingsChanged but no onContentChanged/Recomputable), and headingStructurallyChanged compares only level/label/numbered (step-inspector.ts:247-249) so a heading TEXT rename (handleRenameHeading = in-place delete+insertText inside the node, editor-ops.ts:130-136) bumps no rev.* counter. parTitle rename (handleRenameParTitle = setNodeMarkup parTitle, editor-ops.ts:166-171) is worse: the attr-step synthesis only handles heading level/label/numbered and figureBlock label/numbered (step-inspector.ts:483-528), never paragraph parTitle, so zero counters bump. After commitRename the pod reverts to displaying {pod.text} (OutlinePanel.tsx:1009) which is derived from extractHeadings(content)←editor.getJSON()←only recomputed on an EditorPane re-render. HOWEVER: the canonical-pane section-path recompute runs on editor.on('update') (EditorLayout.tsx:2127-2134) and setStates when any active-breadcrumb entry's TEXT changes (compares v.text===path[i].text, EditorLayout.tsx:2104-2110). So renaming a heading that is CURRENTLY in the active section path forces a re-render and the outline refreshes immediately — masking the bug in the common 'edit the section you're looking at' case. Renaming a heading NOT in the active breadcrumb, or any parTitle (parTitle text is not in the section path), is NOT masked → reliably stale. This is exactly the finder's medium-confidence caveat, now resolved by code. No data loss (the rename DID land in the .tex/doc; only the panel label is stale) and recoverable by any subsequent structural edit, so MEDIUM not higher.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Same no-counter-bump root as the finder (in-place text edit + untracked parTitle attr fire no DocStructureBus event the rev.* counters listen to: step-inspector.ts:247-249, 483-528; useStructuralRevisions.ts:93-128), AND the EditorPane content snapshot (editor.getJSON(), EditorPane.tsx:3400/3473) only recomputes on re-render. The corrected nuance: the staleness is intermittently masked by the section-path recompute's text-keyed setState (EditorLayout.tsx:2104-2110, fired from on('update') at :2127-2134) for headings sitting in the live active breadcrumb; it is NOT masked for off-screen headings or for any parTitle (parTitle text never enters the section path).
verdicts.class: Derived/memoized views sourced from editor.getJSON() that must reflect an edit firing no structural counter: outline word-count + section-number columns ride the same `content` snapshot; live heading-row text fails to update while typing a heading title directly in the main editor (same path, partially masked by the section-path recompute). Deeper class: 'in-place text / untracked-attr edits that no structural counter observes, consumed by a counter-gated render.'

verdicts.rationale: Confirmed by direct trace. allRowAttrs includes parTitle rows as draggable snap candidates (OutlinePanel.tsx:1244-1246) and the drag flush calls onSnapBoundary(edge, rows[bestIdx].blockIndex) with the raw block index of the snapped row (OutlinePanel.tsx:1326). In useFocusMode.snapBoundary the TOP edge uses blockIndex directly as the new start (bandFromIndices(doc, blockIndex, cur.endIdx,...), useFocusMode.ts:363-365) → exact-paragraph snap, while the BOTTOM edge routes through sectionRange(blockIndex, headings, totalBlocks) and uses newEnd (useFocusMode.ts:367-369). For a parTitle blockIndex, sectionRange finds no matching heading (findIndex===-1, line 133), falls to the enclosing-heading branch (lines 149-153) and recurses → returns the WHOLE enclosing section's [start,end], so the bottom edge jumps to the section end, not the dropped paragraph. The 'if (blockIndex < cur.startIdx) return s' guard (line 367) does not fire for the repro (dropping mid-section, blockIndex>=startIdx). Asymmetry real. LOW: requires Show-par-titles + unlocked focus + dragging the bottom handle specifically onto a parTitle row; purely a focus-band view nuance, fully recoverable, no data impact.
verdicts.class: Boundary operations that round one edge through sectionRange and pass the other edge as a raw index. nudgeBoundary (useFocusMode.ts:318-349) repeats the identical top=raw / bottom=sectionRange split and would inherit the asymmetry if its keyboard wiring is ever enabled (currently unwired — verified: only snapBoundary is called from OutlinePanel).

verdicts.rationale: Confirmed. EditorMirror is a second EditorView bound to the SAME EditorState ('multiple views, one state', EditorMirror.tsx:4-10,57-67) — there is exactly one shared selection. handleScrollToHeading's split bottom-pane branch calls editor.commands.setTextSelection(1) for docstart (editor-ops.ts:60) and setTextSelection(pos) for a heading (editor-ops.ts:72) on the CANONICAL editor before scrolling the mirror DOM; that selection transaction mutates the shared state, so the top pane's caret/selection silently relocates to the jump target even though the user only intended to navigate the bottom pane. The user perceives it on returning to the top pane (caret no longer where they left it). LOW is correct: only reachable in split-pane mode with the bottom pane active, no content mutated, fully recoverable by clicking back into the top pane. Finder's 'medium' confidence is conservative; mechanism is unambiguous so I rate the verdict high-confidence, severity LOW.
verdicts.class: Jump/scroll handlers that set the single shared editor selection as a means of moving a secondary mirror view. Any panel jump routed to the mirror via the same setTextSelection-on-shared-state pattern perturbs the main pane caret; the docstart and heading branches (editor-ops.ts:59-63, 71-80) are the two concrete sites.
